newsitem.title: USA: Calif. Gov. signs bill to protect bond investors.
newsitem.headline: Calif. Gov. signs bill to protect bond investors.

text.p: California Gov. Pete Wilson on Tuesday signed legislation to protect municipal bond investors in the event state and local government officials make minor mistakes in bond offering documents.

The so-called Validating Act signed by Wilson ensures that minor errors in bond documents do not undermine the legal integrity of the bonds. The act only applies to typographical, grammatical and procedural errors or omissions in bond documents.
Without the act, bond counsels would be reluctant to certify public agency bonds as good risks because there might be mistakes that could invalidate future payments.
Validating acts are renewed each year by state lawmakers.
